Ready to stop reporting on the business and start influencing it?

Some finance roles are all about producing reports. This isn't one of them.

At MiHaven, we're looking for a Financial Controller who wants a seat at the table. Someone who sees beyond the numbers, challenges the status quo and isn't afraid to ask, "There has to be a better way."

You'll work directly with our Directors, lead a small finance team and become the commercial voice behind some of our biggest business decisions.

If you're looking for a role where you can genuinely influence the future of a growing business, not just report on it,you've just found it!

The Opportunity

It's not your typical Financial Controller position. Yes, you'll oversee the finance function. Yes, you'll manage budgets, forecasts, cash flow and reporting.

But you'll also be responsible for helping shape the financial success of major construction projects, providing the commercial insight that keeps projects on track and ensuring every dollar works harder for the business.

We're looking for someone who's curious. Someone who challenges. Someone who sees opportunities where others see spreadsheets. You can check out the day to day via the PD which is located on our careers page.

About You

You might already be a Financial Controller. Or perhaps you're the Finance Manager who's already doing the work but hasn't been given the title. Either way, you'll bring:

    Strong commercial acumen
    Exceptional financial reporting and forecasting skills
    Confidence leading people and holding your team accountable
    The ability to influence operational leaders
    A proactive mindset focused on improving systems and processes
    The confidence to speak up, challenge ideas and contribute strategically

Construction experience would be great,but it's not essential.

Commercial thinking is.
Why you'll love this role

This is one of those rare opportunities where your contribution won't disappear into layers of management.

Your work will be seen.

Your ideas will be heard.

Your decisions will make a difference.

You'll enjoy:

    Negotiable salary based on experience
    Option to include company vehicle and/or fuel card as part of remuneration package
    On-site parking
    Full-time office-based role in Cairns
    Genuine autonomy
    Direct access to the Directors
    The opportunity to build something better

If you're ready to step into a role where you'll influence decisions not just report on them, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, connect with our Recruitment Business Partner Victoria Williams on 03 9691 4712.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 






Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.



To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.


Corporate Applications Enablement Manager




Strategic leadership role driving optimisation and value realisation across Monash Health's corporate systems landscape. 


Lead business improvement initiatives across Oracle Fusion, UKG Dimensions and SuccessFactors.


Permanent, full-time role, based at Scoresby Corporate Site.





About the Role


Monash Health is the largest healthcare provider in Victoria and is recognised for its exceptional clinical care and research. We are dedicated to providing outstanding patient care. We appreciate our unique and vital role as an integral part of the communities we serve and the importance of maintaining our services in a changing environment. The integrity and optimisation of our corporate systems are critical to our ability to deliver excellent care to every patient, every time.


This role represents an exciting leadership opportunity within our Corporate Applications and Enablement function. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Corporate Applications & Enablement, you will be responsible for driving continuous business improvement, optimisation and value realisation across Monash Health's key corporate enterprise systems, with a particular focus on Oracle Fusion, UKG Dimensions and SuccessFactors. 


Working closely with senior leaders, Payroll, Finance, People & Culture, Digital Health and external vendors, you will play a critical role in ensuring corporate systems are aligned to organisational strategy, support operational excellence and deliver measurable business outcomes. 


If appointed, your contribution will be assessed across five Key Result Areas:




Business Improvement and Optimisation


Corporate Systems Ownership and Stewardship


Stakeholder Engagement and Change Management


Governance, Risk and Compliance


Leadership and Capability Uplift




This role is expected to work in a hybrid model, with a minimum of three days per week on site in our Scoresby Office.



About You


The Corporate Applications Enablement Manager ensures that Monash Health's corporate systems continue to evolve, improve and deliver value to the organisation. You are a strategic thinker who enjoys partnering with business leaders to identify opportunities, solve complex problems and drive transformational change.


You possess exceptional stakeholder engagement skills and have demonstrated success influencing senior leaders and cross-functional teams. You understand how technology, people and process come together to deliver sustainable business outcomes and can confidently lead initiatives that improve operational performance and user experience. 


Naturally collaborative and results-focused, you have a passion for continuous improvement and enjoy creating environments where teams can thrive, innovate and deliver meaningful outcomes.


On a personal level, you are:




A strategic and innovative thinker


Highly organised and outcomes focused


An effective communicator who can influence at all levels of the organisation


A trusted advisor with strong stakeholder management skills


Passionate about continuous improvement and organisational capability uplift


A collaborative and empowering leader who brings out the best in others





What You Need



To be considered for this role, you will need to demonstrate:




Tertiary qualification in Business, Information Technology, Human Resources, Finance or a related discipline


Significant experience leading business improvement, process optimisation or enterprise systems initiatives in a complex organisation


Experience working with corporate enterprise systems such as Oracle Fusion, SuccessFactors, UKG Dimensions or similar platforms


Demonstrated ability to develop business cases, executive reports and governance submissions


Proven experience leading organisational change, stakeholder engagement and adoption activities


Strong understanding of governance, risk management and compliance frameworks


Experience working across multiple business functions including Finance, Payroll and People & Culture


Demonstrated leadership experience, including mentoring, coaching and developing team capability. 



While not mandatory requirements, experience with the following will be highly regarded:




Healthcare or public sector experience


Large-scale enterprise transformation programs


Business process redesign and continuous improvement frameworks


Vendor management and external partnership management


Data-driven decision making and business performance improvement initiatives. 



We are especially interested in hearing from candidates who have successfully enabled business transformation through enterprise systems and who are passionate about creating better experiences for both customers and employees.



Benefits of Working at Monash Health



Monash Health offers a range of benefits, including:




Comprehensive employee health and wellbeing programs including Fitness Passport


Five weeks annual leave with leave loading


Monthly ADOs for full-time employees


Salary packaging benefits


Flexible and hybrid working arrangements


Professional development and leadership opportunities


The opportunity to influence large-scale workforce, payroll and financial systems supporting one of Australia's largest health services



For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Sherree O'Connell, Head of Corporate Applications and Enablement on 0451 309 776

Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement.

USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client Star Steel Structures & Frames Pty Ltd (SSSF), ABN: 52 630 055 248 located at: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760 is a Premier Steel supply and installation company. It is a 100% Australian owned company that provides customisable solutions in high-quality reinforcing mesh, structural steel, and prefabrication services, specializing in eco-friendly construction materials. They focus on delivering durable, moisture-resistant, and heat-resistant products made from 100% recyclable steel. With a commitment to sustainability, Star steel ensures a 48-hour turnaround for quotes while adhering to Australian construction standards. Their products are designed for maximum efficiency and reliability, serving the needs of construction professionals who value quality and eco-conscious solutions.

Due to the business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit Welder(s) in their Operations team on a permanent full-time basis. We are seeking an experienced Welder or maybe two, to join our operations team on a full-time basis. The successful candidate will be responsible for fabricating, joining, and repairing metal components and structures using a range of welding techniques, working from technical drawings and specifications to produce high-quality, structurally sound welds in accordance with the relevant Australian standards.

Position: Welder
No of positions: 02
Reports to: Operations Head / Supervisor
Location: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760
Annual salary range: AUD $80,000 - $85,000 base + Super (for a 38-hour work week)

As a Welder, your main duties and responsibilities includes:
•	Ensuring all work is carried out in compliance with WHS regulations and relevant Australian Standards.
•	Cutting, bending, shaping, joining and repairing metal components of iron and steel structures, boilers, pressure vessels and pipes.
•	Studying blueprints, drawings and specifications to determine job requirements.
•	Selecting, cleaning and preparing metal stock.
•	Cutting marked-out metal sections and shapes using hand tools, flame cutting torches and metal cutting machines.
•	Shaping and bending metal sections and pipes using hand and machine tools and by heating and hammering.
•	Aligning parts to be joined using hand tools and measuring instruments.
•	Joining metal sections using various welding techniques, bolting and riveting.
•	Examining welds for width of bead, penetration and precision.
•	Finishing products by cleaning, polishing, filing and bathing in acidic solutions. 
•	Cleaning and smoothing welds by filing, chiselling and grinding.
•	Selecting and applying appropriate welding processes (manual metal arc, gas metal arc, advanced welding techniques) based on material and job specifications.
•	 Assembling fabricated components in line with technical drawings.
•	Applying safe welding practices and maintaining accurate weld records.
•	Operating fixed and mobile load-shifting equipment at workshop as required.
•	Working safely and effectively within manufacturing and engineering environments, complying with WHS and environmental sustainability requirements. 
•	Performing engineering measurements, inspections and quality checks on completed welds and fabricated items.
•	Ordering materials and planning work activities to meet production schedules.
•	Organising and communicating information with supervisors and team members. 
•	Using hand tools, power tools and computing technology relevant to fabrication and welding tasks.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Engineering - Fabrication Trade – Welder (First class) preferred.
•	At least 5 years of proven work experience in the above job role. 
•	Sound welding experience in manual / advanced metal arc welding & Gas metal arc welding process. 
•	Well experienced of WHS requirements, particularly in manufacturing and steel fabrication environment. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.

Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask and physically fit
•	Process and results driven 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive & hard-working

Additional information: 
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when delivering key orders. 
•	Ability to travel interstate if required
